numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For coarser-resolution downcasts, the implementation previously used `pc.cast(..., safe=False)`, which truncates toward zero and can silently wrap on int64 overflow. This produced incorrect rounding for negative durations/pre-epoch timestamps and silently returned int64-wrapped garbage instead of raising on out-of-bounds upcasts.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Match numpy/pandas `as_unit`: floor toward −inf for downcasts (direction-aware) and raise `OutOfBoundsDatetime`/`OutOfBoundsTimedelta` on overflow/out-of-bounds instead of silently wrapping.
trigger_conditions: Negative timedeltas/durations where truncation toward zero differs from floor toward −inf (e.g., converting −93784567890123ns to seconds).
Pre-epoch timestamps crossing the epoch boundary when converting to a coarser unit (e.g., 1969-12-31 23:59:59.123456789ns to seconds).
oracle_clues: Regression from GH-63573 switching `ArrowExtensionArray._dt_as_unit` to `pc.cast(..., safe=False)`.
`pc.cast` with `safe=False` truncates toward zero and can silently wrap on int64 overflow.

Fix requirement stated: downcasts must floor toward −inf via int64 arithmetic; same/finer resolution casts use `safe=True` so overflow raises `OutOfBoundsDatetime`/`OutOfBoundsTimedelta` instead of wrapping.
Code comment explicitly notes the bug cause: `pc.cast` truncates toward zero, wrong for negative timedeltas and pre-epoch timestamps (GH#63573).

category_specific_evidence: Regression GH-63573 switched `ArrowExtensionArray._dt_as_unit` to `pc.cast(..., safe=False)`, which truncates toward zero and silently wraps on int64 overflow.
Mathematical property violated: numpy/pandas `as_unit` must floor toward −inf, not truncate toward zero (flooring direction-aware downcast needed).
Negative duration example: `-93784567890123ns -> s` gave `-93784s` instead of `-93785s`.
Out-of-bounds upcast overflow example: year-2600 `timestamp[s] -> ns` silently returned int64-wrapped garbage instead of raising.
Fix requirement: downcasts floor toward −inf via int64 arithmetic; overflow must raise `OutOfBoundsDatetime`/`OutOfBoundsTimedelta` instead of wrapping.

Evidence of overflow-raise requirements in tests: `timestamp[s][pyarrow]` with `pd.Timestamp("2600-01-01").as_unit("s")` must raise `OutOfBoundsDatetime` when calling `ser.dt.as_unit("ns")` (match="overflow").
Evidence of overflow-raise requirements in tests: `duration[s][pyarrow]` with value `19880899200` must raise `OutOfBoundsTimedelta` when calling `ser.dt.as_unit("ns")` (match="overflow").
Evidence of floor-vs-truncate behavior in test comments: `test_as_unit_duration_negative_floors` asserts downcasting negative durations must floor toward −inf like numpy, not truncate toward zero.
Concrete values used for negative duration test: `values = [93784567890123, -93784567890123, None]` converted from ns then downcast across units using `ser_arrow.dt.as_unit(to_unit)`.
reproduction_risks: Reproducing the truncation/overflow requires exercising the `safe=False` code path (historical behavior) or the pre-fix implementation that used `pc.cast(..., safe=False)`.
Overflow behavior depends on int64 overflow wrapping; specific out-of-bounds examples (e.g., year 2600, duration value 19880899200) may be required to trigger it as described.
Correctness depends on downcast direction (coarser resolution) so using in-range/positive values may not demonstrate the bug, as noted.
